chunks: Eat of what God has provided you, lawful and good, and be grateful for the bounty of God, if you truly worship Him.
ai.seo_question: What is the connection between eating lawful food and worshipping God in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah An-Nahl is often cited to establish the dual criteria of halal (permissibility) and tayyib (purity/quality) for sustenance, emphasizing that mere legality is insufficient without spiritual and physical purity. It elevates the mundane act of eating to an act of worship (ibadah), linking physical nourishment directly to gratitude (shukr) and the recognition of God’s providence, a concept central to the Shia understanding of daily life as a continuum of devotion.
